rationale: Full-text Spanish comparative descriptive/observational study analyzing official administrative, surveillance, and household survey data (2015-2016) on drinking-water access in Panama and Costa Rica. Mechanistically, the study centrally compares (1) utility/operator models and independent regulator scope (regulatory_model_ownership: national utilities IDAAN/AyA, municipal utilities, public enterprise ESPH, private concessions, and rural community boards JAARs/CS and CAAR/ASADAS in Cuadros 1-3, plus urban-only ASEP regulation in Panama vs nationwide non-municipal ARESEP regulation in Costa Rica), alongside co-equally prominent analysis of (2) regulatory water-quality standard application and compliance surveillance (enforcement_sanctions: Panama's outdated Reglamento Tecnico DGNTI-COPANIT 23-395-99 excluding rural aqueducts vs Costa Rica's universal Decreto Ejecutivo 38924-S and PNMSCSAP Decreto Ejecutivo 33953-S-MINAET) and (3) fragmented sector stewardship and urban/rural mandate splits (institutional_structure_coordination: ASEP vs DISAPAS and weak, fractioned rectoria). Outcomes are co-equally split between household piped network connection coverage (primary_connection: 94.6% vs 97.6% piped supply and Cuadro 4 dwelling tap status) and potable water quality/service quality (effective_access: 74.6% vs 91.8% potable water coverage in Cuadros 2 and 7).
